text:
olivia: quick thread — we need a decision on who owns the "prefetch window" by default for SDKs (python/ts/go). server-side? sdk-side? opt-in only? tradeoffs outlined below.

mike: +1 to discuss. iirc the current server does automatic prefetch for small windows but clients also do naive prefetching. leads to double work sometimes.

sara: i'm leaning toward server-owned default with an opt-out flag in SDKs. reasons: 1) centralized telemetry/knobs, 2) easier to enforce global limits (cost/sla).

raj: counterpoint: server-owned prefetch can hide client workload patterns and makes offline/embedded private deployments harder. for private deployments we want client-local defaults.

olivia: good points. what about a compromise: server-owned default for hosted, but SDKs expose same opt-in API so Dedicated/Private can flip to client-first? keep surface identical but default differs by environment.

casey: surfaced API shape suggestion (keeps parity across langs):
```
// config (pseudo)
client = RedwoodClient({
  prefetch: {
    mode: "auto", // auto/server|client|disabled
    window_tokens: 256,
  }
})
```
globals: mode = "auto" resolves to server when hosting metadata present, else client-local.

mike: that API looks fine ergonomically. two followups: 1) who implements backoff/retry when prefetch hits rate limits? 2) how do we avoid double-prefetching (client + server) when mode=auto and client SDK old?

sara: answers: 1) backoff/retry belongs to the component doing the prefetch; if server owns prefetch, server's rate limiter/backoff applies. but SDK should still implement idempotent cancel+resume so clients can recover gracefully. 2) we need a capability header from server: `x-prefetch-handled: true` so SDK detects and disables client prefetch fallback for that request. small versioned handshake.

raj: +1 for capability header. but consider transport choices — streaming vs unary prefetch control. streaming lets server push prefetch hints, unary needs extra roundtrip. for low-latency apps streaming is better but heavier to implement in some SDKs.

olivia: true. for Python/TS/Go we need a minimal interop plan. propose: default to unary headers + a single optional control gRPC stream for long-lived sessions. SDKs can opt into stream if user opens a `Session` object.

casey: implementation sketch for go/python:
```
// python: session = client.open_session(prefetch_stream=True)
// ts: const session = client.session({prefetchStream: true})
```
session opens the control stream and listens for `prefetch_window_adjust` events.

mike: how do retries interact? if prefetch is speculative we may consume tokens then fail — who accounts for that cost and how to roll back?

sara: we should make speculative-prefetch tokens billable only if actually used by model. tracking needs per-token attribution. fallback: conservative default window so wasted tokens minimal. also add telemetry label `prefetch_speculative=true/false`.

raj: long-term refactor note: we should consolidate prefetch + kv-cache API into a single "local cache policy" module in SDKs so different prefetch strategies (sequential, speculative, LRU) can be swapped without changing higher-level API.

olivia: agreed — add to roadmap: "cache/prefetch policy refactor" Q3. short term: agree to server-owned default for hosted, sdk opt-out flag, capability header, unary header + optional control stream, conservative window=128 tokens.

casey: i'll open a tiny RFC PR with the API examples, header names, and a backwards-compatible handshake. will include sample migration notes for existing SDKs.

mike: :thumbsup: also add e2e test plan — simulate old SDK + new server to ensure no double-prefetch and safe fallthrough.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: created issue INFR-2145: "prefetch ownership defaults + sdk handshake" assigned to @casey.

olivia: thanks all. tagging followups: @sara please spec telemetry labels, @raj please draft session stream wireproto, @mike add e2e tests.

sara: will do.

raj: drafting proto now, will ping for review in ~2h.

casey: RFC PR up: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/701 — feedback welcome.

olivia: perfect. closing thread for now, reopen in sync channel if we need real-time sync. :rocket:
